brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Kilnroom, the online shop in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: handmade and warm but not rustic or folksy; no pottery wheels, no vase or mug silhouettes, no flames. It must work on a shipping label, a tissue-paper sticker and Instagram. Web and social only; customers in Turkey and Europe.

claim.notes: All three concepts (maker-stamp, doorway, glaze-tiles) failed the critic's quality gate after two rounds, so nothing was finalized, exported or installed and no gallery was built.

concepts.title: Opening Doorway
readsAs: a sail beside a dark panel (sailing/yacht brand)
a door swung open - the generic exit/log-out UI icon
an open book or folded leaflet. Unfortunate: a marine or travel-booking mark, or a 'sign out' button
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 arched door/window with a lit slot (also: tombstone, mailbox slot); s2 horseshoe magnet or a plain door icon; s3 igloo / bread oven, and the kiln is drawn plainly (struck); s4 lowercase r or a periscope, a different letter (struck); s5 a split arch, the struck cut device, also a pair of gravestones. Keep s1: the only one where the idea (the kiln door opening onto warm light) comes first, and the off-centre sliver is the ownable part. Fix: the generic boutique arch and the tombstone reading are the risks. Make the outer form less of a stock half-pill (flatter, kiln-brick shoulder or slightly hand-drawn proportion), give the sliver a deliberate shape (taper or a soft lean, as if the door is just ajar) so it reads as light, not a slot, and check one-colour: the sliver must hold as a knockout without the terracotta.

concepts.title: Glaze Run
readsAs: paint dripping over a globe (Sherwin-Williams 'Cover the Earth')
a circuit trace with pin terminals
a melting ice-cream scoop or a face - unfortunate: a paint brand or a melting/damaged item for a breakage-insured shop
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a disc dipped in something that runs: dripping paint or a chocolate-dipped biscuit, glaze on a second look; the two drips also read as rounded teeth / 'uu' (a ghost or jellyfish at 16 px); s2 a ring with a hook or keyhole poking into the hole, a toggle/power-ish glyph; the drip does not read as glaze (struck: idea not visible); s3 a medicine capsule/pill (struck: pharma/UI cliche); s4 a two-tone circle split by a wave, generic stock shape (0.87) and Pepsi-adjacent (struck). Keep s1: the only sketch where a stranger sees dipping and running. Fix: the drips are parallel U-shaped columns of equal width, which looks like teeth and generic paint-drip clip art. Make them real glaze runs: unequal lengths and widths, tapering from the edge, ending in a heavier rounded bead, one clearly dominant; make the dip edge less even, with a slight tilt, as in a hand dip. Avoid melting/slime drip cliches (no more than two runs, no splash). Stock-shape similarity is 0.81, so the run silhouette has to carry the ownability. The one-colour label version must hold via the paper gap line alone. Check that the 16 px render reads as a dipped disc, not a face.

concepts.title: Maker's Stamp
readsAs: a camera lens or webcam app icon
a record button / ring-in-squircle UI glyph
a fried egg or a stone with a pebble. Unfortunate: an Instagram-style camera icon on the very Instagram avatar it must work as
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a bowling ball (struck); s2 a seal with an oval dimple and a small hole, loosely a button or a zero; s3 a refresh/loading spiral, a UI icon (struck); s4 a target, an eye or a bowl from above (struck); s5 claw or scratch marks, which suggests damage for a brand selling breakage insurance (struck). Keep s2: the press-into-clay idea at least survives, and the asymmetric pool plus small hole is the least stock combination. Risks: the oval in a circle reads as 0 or a seed, and the small circle reads as a stray dot or a bite. Fix: make the pool clearly a finger press (one soft, asymmetric edge where the clay was pushed up, not a clean ellipse), justify the hole (a hanging/stamp hole) or remove it, and give the outer seal a slightly irregular edge that still looks refined, not rustic.
